Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Key facts:
- Certificate number: R76/2006-FR2-16.02 rev.0
- Issuing authority: Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d'Essais (LNE)
- Person responsible: Thomas LOMMATZSCH, Responsable du Pôle Certification / Measuring Instruments Division Manager
- Address: 1, rue Gaston Boissier - 75724 Paris Cedex 15
- Phone: 01 40 43 37 00, Fax: 01 40 43 37 37, E-mail: info@lne.fr, Website: www.lne.fr

- Manufacturer: PRECIA SA BP 106, FRA 07001 PRIVAS CEDEX
- Certified type: Non automatic weighing instrument type P1401-A → category "Non automatic weighing instrument" (or "Instrument"). The schema example categories: "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system", "Fuel dispenser", "Taximeter", "Gas meter", ... So category could be "Non-automatic weighing instrument". Type designation: P1401-A.
- Module designation: analogic data processing unit type X1309-TR — that's a component. The terminal is e.g. X1301 (covered by another certificate R76/2006-FR2-15.01).
- Accuracy class III.
- Recommendation: R76, edition 2006. Scheme? The certificate number R76/2006-FR2-16.02. The scheme field in certificate: scheme (A|B). Hmm — this is an OIML-MAA certificate ("ANNEXE au CERTIFICAT OIML-MAA"). MAA certificates... The schema says scheme (A|B). For basic certificates the scheme is typically not given; MAA cert... Not clearly A or B. The certificate title says "CERTIFICAT OIML DE CONFORMITE" and annex says "Appendix to OIML-MAA CERTIFICATE". MAA = Mutual Acceptance Arrangement, which is "MAA". Scheme A|B doesn't apply directly; I'll omit scheme or leave null. Rules say don't fabricate — omit.

- Date issued: 2016-04-15 ("Issued on April 15th, 2016")
- Member state: FRANCE
- Page total: 2
- project_number: "CIM16b-VC45-2013"? That's at top — it's an internal reference. Hmm, project_number — not clearly. Maybe omit. Actually "CIM16b-VC45-2013" could be a project/file number. I'll include it as project_number since it appears prominently. Hmm, risk of fabrication. It's ambiguous but it is present in the doc. I'll include it.
- oiml_issuer_id: not present explicitly. Omit.

Test reports:
- LNE n° P152515 – Document DMSI/1 (performance tests, influence factors tests and span stability tests – 51 pages) → test_report, pages 51
- LNE n° P152515 - Document DE/2 (Disturbances tests – 17 pages) → note discrepancy: first list says LNE n° P152515 – Document DE/2, English says P133689 - Document DE/2. I'll use P152515 (French original), maybe note? Just pick one; French authoritative. id: "LNE P152515 - Document DE/2", pages 17, role test_report.
- LNE-P152515-PCI/3 (Evaluation report – 14 pages) → role evaluation_report, pages 14.

Revision history: rev.0 — "revision": "0". Date: 2016-04-15. Changes: null/omit.

Characteristics:
- Accuracy class: III
- Number of weighing ranges: 2
- Range 1: Max1 = 3 kg, Min1 = 20 g, e1 = 1 g
- Range 2: Max2 = 30 kg, Min2 = 100 g, e2 = 5 g
- For transport tariff instruments: Range 1: Max1 = 3 kg, Min1 = 5 g, e1 = 1 g; Range 2: Max2 = 30 kg, Min2 = 25 g, e2 = 5 g
- Maximum tare effect: T = -Max
- Temperature range: +10 °C / +40 °C

This is a config-level variation: two configurations (standard vs transport-tariff instruments). Use config_level with axis "instrument_usage" (standard vs transport_tariff).

config_level entries:
- attribute: minimum_capacity, axis: weighing_range, values: [{condition: "range_1", value: 20 g}, {condition: "range_2", value: 100 g}, {condition: "range_1 transport_tariff", value: 5 g}, {condition: "range_2 transport_tariff", value: 25 g}]

Hmm, but Max and e are same across configurations; Min varies. Two config axes could be combined: axis "application" with conditions "standard/range_1" etc. Let me structure:

config_level: [
  {attribute: "maximum_capacity", axis: "weighing_range", values: [{condition: "range_1", value: 3, unit_symbol: "kg"}, {condition: "range_2", value: 30, unit_symbol: "kg"}]},
  {attribute: "minimum_capacity", axis: "application|weighing_range", values: [
    {condition: "standard range_1", value: 20, unit_symbol: "g"},
    {condition: "standard range_2", value: 100, unit_symbol: "g"},
    {condition: "transport_tariff range_1", value: 5, unit_symbol: "g"},
    {condition: "transport_tariff range_2", value: 25, unit_symbol: "g"}
  ]},
  {attribute: "verification_scale_interval", axis: "weighing_range", values: [{condition: "range_1", value: 1, unit_symbol: "g"}, {condition: "range_2", value: 5, unit_symbol: "g"}]},
  {attribute: "maximum_tare_effect", axis: null, values: [{condition: null, value: "-Max", ...}]} — T = -Max is a formula → value string "-Max".
  {attribute: "temperature_range", ...} — could be type_level: value {min: 10, max: 40}, unit °C. Actually -10/+40 is typical but here it's +10/+40. Yes doc says +10 °C / +40 °C.

type_level:
- accuracy_class: "III"
- number_of_weighing_ranges: 2
- temperature_range: {min: 10, max: 40}, "°C"
- maximum_tare_effect: value "T = -Max" or "-Max" string. I'll record as {value: "-Max", unit_symbol: null} with attribute "maximum_tare_effect". Formula kept as string.

Components:
- role: "analogic data processing unit", type_designations: ["X1309-TR"]
- role: "terminal (indicating module)", type_designations: ["X1301"], with characteristics noting example certificate R76/2006-FR2-15.01, alternatives? "exemple: type X1301" — so terminal module is any PRECIA-compatible terminal with OIML-MAA certificate; example X1301. Record as component with characteristic reference_certificate: "R76/2006-FR2-15.01".

model_family: only one model P1401-A, so omit model_family.

module_designation: schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. The instrument is composed of an analogic data processing unit X1309-TR + terminal. Module designation maybe "Analog weighing module"? Hmm. For R76 modular instruments: the X1309-TR is an analogic data processing unit. I'd set module_designation to null and record components. Or "Analogic data processing unit"? The schema examples are for load cells. I'll set null and use components.

Recommendation: id "R76", edition 2006, amendment null, accuracy_classes ["III"].

Certificate:

- scheme: omit (MAA cert, not A/B basic). Actually OIML-MAA certificates — the MAA has categories... The schema restricts scheme to A|B. Since not stated, omit.
